audit.whatIsWrong: mid says 'At 6 respect Purgatory: your R is a clean engage but he can execute you back'. Purgatory carries grounding as well as the execute — Riot: 'Locke throws a binding artifact that deals damage and potentially executes enemies hit.', kit flags grounding, slow, execute.
audit.why: The entry treats his ult as a damage race you might lose. It is worse than that: grounding shuts off dashes, and Unstoppable Force is a dash. His 120s ultimate can take your 130s ultimate off the table before the execute is even relevant, which changes the order of the two ults from 'trade' to 'his goes first or yours does not go at all'.
audit.corrected: Purgatory grounds — it can strip Unstoppable Force out of your engage, not just execute you afterwards.

audit.whatIsWrong: Soul Ignition is never named or described. Riot: 'Locke ignites his soul, gaining Attack Speed and Move Speed, and dealing damage to himself. At the end of the duration, Locke will heal back a portion of the damage he takes during the effect.' It also carries true damage.
audit.why: Two consequences, neither present. The healing is deferred to the end of the window, so Grievous Wounds applied during it — not after — is what decides an extended trade, and this entry's whole plan is extended trades. And the true damage means the armour wall the page keeps promising does not cover everything he throws.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds applied inside Soul Ignition's window cuts the payback; its true damage ignores your armour.

audit.whatIsWrong: Not one of Locke's abilities except Purgatory is named. The poke is called 'mark poke' and 'on-hit poke' throughout; the entry never says Ritual Nails, Silver Stake or Ashen Pursuit.
audit.why: The mark mechanic is specific and actionable: Ritual Nails marks at 950 range on a 10s cooldown at rank 1 and he then consumes those marks with attacks, so the danger is not the nail landing, it is him reaching you afterwards. Silver Stake's on-hit scales with your missing health, which is why the chip accelerates as the lane goes on. And Ashen Pursuit is a 10s dash with an auto reset — Ground Slam's grounding denies it.
audit.corrected: Ritual Nails, Silver Stake and Ashen Pursuit named, with Ground Slam grounding the dash.
sources: champ-data/_kits/locke.json (P Silver Stake, Q Ritual Nails, E Ashen Pursuit)

audit.whatIsWrong: All three spike texts are generic — 'his mark burst', 'his on-hit poke', 'a fight-swinging R he cannot out-race'. The last is wrong on its face given Purgatory's grounding.
audit.why: Calling your R something he cannot out-race is the exact opposite of the interaction. Restating the three spikes on named abilities keeps the timing and makes each one checkable.
audit.corrected: Spikes rewritten on Thunderclap/Ritual Nails, Silver Stake and Purgatory's grounding.

audit.why: Skill through level 3, Malphite from the first item on, matches 51.78% over 1408 games and matches the prose. No chart change proposed.

edits.before: The first three levels are a genuine skill lane: trade Q for his mark poke, step out of range to reset Granite Shield between exchanges, and do not burn your mana bar racing him — neither of you can actually force a kill yet, so the winner here is whoever banks more free chip and CS.
edits.after: The first three levels are a genuine skill lane: trade Seismic Shard for Ritual Nails (950 range, 10s at rank 1), step out to reset Granite Shield between exchanges, and do not burn mana racing him — neither of you forces a kill yet, so the winner is whoever banks more free chip and CS.

edits.before: From 4-5 your W, first armor points and passive start blunting his burst, so shove and chip him with Q on cooldown. At 6 respect Purgatory: your R is a clean engage but he can execute you back, so ult for ganks or when his R is down. After first item you flat out-sustain his on-hit poke and the lane is yours.
edits.after: From 4-5 Thunderclap, armor points and Granite Shield blunt his burst, so chip with Seismic Shard every 8s. At 6 respect Purgatory (120s): it grounds, so it does not just execute you, it strips Unstoppable Force from your engage. Ult after his R. After first item you out-sustain Silver Stake's on-hit chip and the lane is yours.

notes: The decisive missing fact is that Purgatory grounds. Locke's 120s ultimate can deny Malphite's 130s dash-ultimate outright, which reverses the entry's framing of the level-6 exchange as an even ult trade. Soul Ignition also needed stating: it heals back a portion of the self-damage at the END of the duration, so Grievous Wounds has to be on him during the window rather than applied afterwards, and its true damage means the armour wall the page promises is not complete. Every ability except Purgatory was unnamed; Ritual Nails, Silver Stake and Ashen Pursuit are now in the text. STRUCTURAL: the packet flags 'spikes[] has 3 entries, expected 4' for this matchup.
